districts.reasoning: Agropastoral cowpea/sorghum district in Middle Shabelle's hinterland, long an insurgent stronghold whose town changed hands in 2019. Livelihood context: Central Cowpea Belt agropastoral zone with low-yield rainfed cowpea/sorghum. Access is sporadic (besieged town or insurgent-held hinterland, road blockades), so treatment coverage and case turnover are limited. Month-to-month variability in new cases is driven by a strongly bimodal gu/deyr harvest cycle with frequent crop failure and repeated blockades that interrupt markets and assistance.

Lower Shabelle riverine farming district on the Afgooye corridor, structurally hosting very large IDP settlements near Mogadishu. Livelihood context: Shabelle/Juba riverine irrigated farming where poor households depend on agricultural labour. Programme presence is concentrated in the district town with partial rural outreach, implying intermediate case turnover; endemic AWD/cholera and measles exposure adds fatality-driven exits. Month-to-month variability in new cases is driven by a bimodal cropping and labour calendar plus AWD/cholera peaks, recurrent river flooding and large, repeated IDP inflows and evictions.

Lower Juba southern inland pastoral district with a government-held town and largely insurgent-influenced rangelands. Month-to-month variability in new cases is driven by drought-sensitive pastoral milk availability and seasonal herd migration and repeated blockades that interrupt markets and assistance.
